startup.name: Sazabi
startup.description: Observability and security platform for fast-moving engineering teams, built around AI. Pitched with backing from founders at AI infrastructure companies. Ten person team in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: Placeholder value only, because Sazabi is already known to be accepted. Test note: accepted to YC, so the acceptance step is not forecast. A ten person team with strong angel names would sit above the roughly 1 percent applicant prior, though observability is crowded.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because observability is a mature, crowded market with Datadog, Grafana and many AI-labeled startups, and AI-native alone is a thin wedge. Endorsements from other founders do not show customers or retention. The interview would test whether the founders can show proof of demand, speed of shipping and a reason the market is open now for Sazabi.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C needs a multi-hundred-million-dollar platform story against Datadog, Coralogix and Grafana. Among the repo analogs none reached C, and most were acquired (HyperDX to ClickHouse, highlight.io to LaunchDarkly), so C is rare. For Sazabi the milestone to reach this round is paying customers and growth that investors can verify, and the analogs listed in this evaluation show that most companies in the cohort miss that bar.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The common end state in the observability analogs is acquisition by a platform at under $100M (HyperDX, highlight.io, Tarsal, Helicone) or a quiet stall (Middleware, SigNoz). Only a few reach a large outcome. Reaching $1B needs to take share from Datadog, which has distribution, a price advantage and an incentive to copy any AI feature.

killers.risk: Free or open source tools anchor price at zero

killers.mitigation: Sell security plus observability together to teams that pay.

killers.evidence: HyperDX, highlight.io, Tarsal and Helicone were all bought at seed stage.
killers.mitigation: Reach $1M of recurring revenue before engaging with acquirers.

killers.risk: Broad scope of observability and security splits focus for ten people

killers.mitigation: Start with one deployment pattern and expand.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingestion, storage and querying of telemetry at scale is well understood, and AI layers rely on third party models. A ten person team can build a usable product, but cost at scale and security detection quality are hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents already add AI agents and have the data and customers. A rival could ship comparable features within months, though a startup can still win in a niche.

narrative.headline: Strong early signals in a crowded market, likely a seed and then a fight for a Series A.
narrative.general_summary: Sazabi pitches an AI-native observability and security platform to fast-moving engineering teams. The team has ten people and strong angel backing, which raises odds of a seed. The market is large and funded, but Datadog, Grafana and Coralogix are adding AI features and open source tools set low prices. Past YC observability companies mostly raised a seed and then were acquired or stalled, so the Series A hinges on paying customers and a sharp wedge. These numbers are wide because the data is a blind description only and the cohorts are small and right censored.
